健康观念变化：年份、十年与三大领域未作答短答题 · 3 段 · 433 词 · 3 题

Academic官方教辅原任务 · Cambridge IELTS Academic Reading Task Type 11 · Changing our Understanding of Health · PDF 第 4, 5 页

Answer the questions below using NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS for each answer. Write your answers in boxes 1–3 on your answer sheet.

原出版社Academic题型教学任务，原题与原教师答案均保留；不标为完整考场试卷。

CIn the late 1940s the World Health Organisation challenged this physically and medically oriented view of health. They stated that "health is a complete state of physical, mental and social well-being and is not merely the absence of disease" (WHO, 1946). Health and the person were seen more holistically (mind/body/spirit) and not just in physical terms.

DThe 1970s was a time of focusing on the prevention of disease and illness by emphasising the importance of the lifestyle and behaviour of the individual. Specific behaviours which were seen to increase risk of disease, such as smoking, lack of fitness and unhealthy eating habits, were targeted. Creating health meant providing not only medical health care, but health promotion programs and policies which would help people maintain healthy behaviours and lifestyles. While this individualistic healthy lifestyles approach to health worked for some (the wealthy members of society), people experiencing poverty, unemployment, underemployment or little control over the conditions of their daily lives benefited little from this approach. This was largely because both the healthy lifestyles approach and the medical approach to health largely ignored the social and environmental conditions affecting the health of people.

EDuring the 1980s and 1990s there has been a growing swing away from seeing lifestyle risks as the root cause of poor health. While lifestyle factors still remain important, health is being viewed also in terms of the social, economic and environmental contexts in which people live. This broad approach to health is called the socio-ecological view of health. The broad socio-ecological view of health was endorsed at the first International Conference of Health Promotion held in 1986, Ottawa, Canada, where people from 38 countries agreed and declared that: "The fundamental conditions and resources for health are peace, shelter, education, food, a viable income, a stable eco-system, sustainable resources, social justice and equity. Improvement in health requires a secure foundation in these basic requirements." (WHO, 1986) It is clear from this statement that the creation of health is about much more than encouraging healthy individual behaviours and lifestyles and providing appropriate medical care. Therefore, the creation of health must include addressing issues such as poverty, pollution, urbanisation, natural resource depletion, social alienation and poor working conditions. The social, economic and environmental contexts which contribute to the creation of heath do not operate separately or independently of each other. Rather, they are interacting and interdependent, and it is the complex interrelationships between them which determine the conditions that promote health. A broad socio-ecological view of health suggests that the promotion of health must include a strong social, economic and environmental focus.

原页文字提示：原题引文保留原页的 creation of heath；上下文讨论健康，自己的表达请写 creation of health。

1. In which year did the World Health Organisation define health in terms of mental, physical and social well-being?

2. Name the three broad areas which relate to people's health, according to the socio-ecological view of health.

3. During which decade were lifestyle risks seen as the major contributors to poor health?

对照答案，回到证据

第 1 题 · 1946

in which year要精确年份1946，不是笼统late 1940s。完整定义用于定位。

(WHO, 1946)

第 2 题 · social, economic, environmental

socio-ecological锁定E段，不能抄C段physical, mental, social。只列三个词，不额外加contexts。

the social, economic and environmental contexts in which people live.

第 3 题 · 1970s

问十年阶段，1970s强调个体生活方式；1980s/1990s已转向更广条件，不能误取转向时间。

The 1970s was a time of focusing on the prevention of disease and illness by emphasising the importance of the lifestyle and behaviour of the individual.

核对原答案页

材料精读 · 内容与词句

三段展示健康观念在材料中的历史扩展：从身体疾病扩展到身心与社会福祉，再从个人行为扩展到人们所处的社会、经济与环境条件。后一种视角补充个人行为和医疗的不足，并未说这些因素不再重要。

C

In the late 1940s the World Health Organisation challenged this physically and medically oriented view of health. They stated that "health is a complete state of physical, mental and social well-being and is not merely the absence of disease" (WHO, 1946). Health and the person were seen more holistically (mind/body/spirit) and not just in physical terms.

C段引述世界卫生组织的健康定义，把健康理解为身体、心理、社会层面的整体福祉，而不仅是没有疾病。were seen和引文年份使这一段具有观念史性质；mind/body/spirit说明整体看待人的取向，不是在提供针对某种疾病的治疗方案。

D

The 1970s was a time of focusing on the prevention of disease and illness by emphasising the importance of the lifestyle and behaviour of the individual. Specific behaviours which were seen to increase risk of disease, such as smoking, lack of fitness and unhealthy eating habits, were targeted. Creating health meant providing not only medical health care, but health promotion programs and policies which would help people maintain healthy behaviours and lifestyles. While this individualistic healthy lifestyles approach to health worked for some (the wealthy members of society), people experiencing poverty, unemployment, underemployment or little control over the conditions of their daily lives benefited little from this approach. This was largely because both the healthy lifestyles approach and the medical approach to health largely ignored the social and environmental conditions affecting the health of people.

D段叙述七十年代重视预防与个人生活方式的取向，包括吸烟、缺乏运动和饮食习惯。文中指出这种方式对不同群体的帮助并不相等：贫困、工作不稳定或难以控制生活条件的人受益有限。问题并非这些人不愿健康，而是方案忽略了影响选择的社会和环境条件。

E

During the 1980s and 1990s there has been a growing swing away from seeing lifestyle risks as the root cause of poor health. While lifestyle factors still remain important, health is being viewed also in terms of the social, economic and environmental contexts in which people live. This broad approach to health is called the socio-ecological view of health. The broad socio-ecological view of health was endorsed at the first International Conference of Health Promotion held in 1986, Ottawa, Canada, where people from 38 countries agreed and declared that: "The fundamental conditions and resources for health are peace, shelter, education, food, a viable income, a stable eco-system, sustainable resources, social justice and equity. Improvement in health requires a secure foundation in these basic requirements." (WHO, 1986) It is clear from this statement that the creation of health is about much more than encouraging healthy individual behaviours and lifestyles and providing appropriate medical care. Therefore, the creation of health must include addressing issues such as poverty, pollution, urbanisation, natural resource depletion, social alienation and poor working conditions. The social, economic and environmental contexts which contribute to the creation of heath do not operate separately or independently of each other. Rather, they are interacting and interdependent, and it is the complex interrelationships between them which determine the conditions that promote health. A broad socio-ecological view of health suggests that the promotion of health must include a strong social, economic and environmental focus.

E段进一步解释社会生态视角，把收入、住房、教育、资源与公平等纳入健康基础。While lifestyle factors still remain important明确保留生活方式的重要性。末尾强调社会、经济、环境条件彼此作用，不是把它们当成三项互不相关的清单；因此促进健康需要同时考虑这些联系。

词语与搭配

not merely the absence of disease

不仅仅是没有疾病

not merely扩展定义而不是否定前项：没有疾病仍相关，但不是对健康的完整说明。

maintain healthy behaviours and lifestyles

维持有益健康的行为和生活方式

maintain强调持续维持；原文同时提醒，个人维持行为的能力受生活条件影响。

the social and environmental conditions

社会与环境条件

conditions在此是人生活的处境与条件，不是合同条款；需说清具体指收入、可达性或周边环境中的哪些因素。

interacting and interdependent

相互作用并且相互依赖

两个并列形容词说明因素间的关系；不是各因素可以分别处理而互不影响。

句子精读

While this individualistic healthy lifestyles approach to health worked for some (the wealthy members of society), people experiencing poverty, unemployment, underemployment or little control over the conditions of their daily lives benefited little from this approach.

虽然这种以个人健康生活方式为中心的做法对一些人——社会中的富裕成员——有效，但经历贫困、失业、就业不足，或很难掌控日常生活条件的人，从中获益很少。

While引出让步，worked for some限制受益范围；people后面的experiencing...修饰处于多种不利处境的人。little指获益很少，不等于严格意义上的零收益；this approach回指强调个人生活方式的取向。

Rather, they are interacting and interdependent, and it is the complex interrelationships between them which determine the conditions that promote health.

相反，这些条件彼此作用、相互依赖，决定有利于健康的条件的，是它们之间复杂的相互关系。

Rather承接前一句，纠正把不同条件当作独立因素的理解；they和them指社会、经济与环境背景。it is...which...是强调结构，突出complex interrelationships，而不是只突出其中单个因素。

这篇材料里可用于写作的表达

the social and environmental conditions

社会与环境条件

适合说明健康行为受到可获得资源与生活环境的影响；必须接具体机制，不把抽象词组当成完整原因。

用于写作：自编例句，直接对应儿童肥胖的原因与措施：把食物和活动空间的可达性作为可以改善的具体条件，不把所有责任归于儿童个人。

maintain healthy behaviours and lifestyles

维持有益健康的行为与生活方式

与提供条件和持续支持搭配；不承诺一项措施可以单独消除儿童肥胖。

用于写作：自编例句，用学校可采取的具体支持回应儿童肥胖题的措施部分；can表示可能贡献，不宣称所有儿童会因此获得相同结果。

读完讲解，可以把原文连起来再读一次；想保留的词句可使用已有收藏功能。
Why we need silence｜噪声风险与城市降噪未作答段落信息匹配 / 人物／特征匹配 · 3 段 · 341 词 · 4 题 · 同篇原文另有裁切

真题 · Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · PDF 第 21 页

Q14–16：Which section contains the following information? 原选项A–G保留，本片段含A–C。Q23：Match the statement with the correct person, A–D. You may use any letter more than once.

AHumans are finely attuned to noise, and for good reason. From an evolutionary perspective, sounds give us vital information, helping us navigate the world and avoid danger. To help ensure loud or unexpected noises get the attention they deserve, our internal chemistry alters in response to them. Our blood pressure goes up, muscles tense and glands release hormones that prepare us for fight or flight. In the short term, this is a good thing. When we are exposed to too much noise over the long term, however, those responses can lead to a multitude of health issues, from sleep disturbance to even cardiovascular disease.

BThe World Health Organization has recently designated excessive noise as an 'underestimated threat' to public health, and has said that people living in cities such as Mumbai, Tokyo and Buenos Aires are being exposed to far more than the recommended 40 decibels of noise at night. A report from the European Environment Agency concluded that noise was an ongoing and widespread issue in Europe, with at least 1 in 5 people consistently exposed to levels considered harmful to health. 'There are no "earlids" that can protect your brain from noise,' says Nick Antonio, an acoustic consultant who has contributed to the British and international standards for noise.

CThe good news is that several cities have been working to turn the volume down. One of the first to do so was London. 'By providing recommendations for quieter buses, reducing noise from roads and also controlling noise from aircraft, they were able to make the city quieter,' says Antonio. Other cities have introduced noise-reducing road coatings, for instance, alongside greenery that muffles sound. Some solutions are more specific: Washington DC's ban on petrol-powered leaf blowers came into effect recently, while in New York City, legislation has been approved to fine people who modify their vehicles to make them noisier. 'People are seeing the benefits of these more quiet environments in their cities,' Antonio says. 'I expect we will see much more of this in the future.'

共用选项 · 原题 14、15、16

  • A
  • B
  • C
  • D
  • E
  • F
  • G

14. examples of strategies to decrease the noise that the public are exposed to

15. data indicating the extent of the problem of excessive noise

16. a description of physiological changes in our bodies when we hear sudden noises

23. The trend towards creating quieter urban locations is likely to increase in the coming years.

  • A Nick Antonio
  • B Justin Feinstein
  • C Tai Dotan Ben-Soussan
  • D Eric Pfeifer

对照答案，回到证据

第 14 题 · C

C列举公交、道路、飞机以及禁令等多项策略；不是只说噪声有害的B。

quieter buses, reducing noise from roads and also controlling noise from aircraft

第 15 题 · B

extent看覆盖范围；1 in 5与城市夜间分贝限制构成具体数据证据。

at least 1 in 5 people consistently exposed to levels considered harmful to health

第 16 题 · A

blood pressure、muscles、glands是身体变化，不是社会影响。

Our blood pressure goes up, muscles tense and glands release hormones

第 23 题 · A

这句话属于Antonio的直接引语，预测降噪趋势继续增加。

I expect we will see much more of this in the future.

核对原答案页

材料精读 · 内容与词句

文章先解释人为什么对声音敏感，再区分短暂警觉的适应价值与长期噪声暴露的健康代价，最后转入城市治理。身体机制、公共健康风险和具体降噪行动形成连续关系。

A

A Humans are finely attuned to noise, and for good reason. From an evolutionary perspective, sounds give us vital information, helping us navigate the world and avoid danger. To help ensure loud or unexpected noises get the attention they deserve, our internal chemistry alters in response to them. Our blood pressure goes up, muscles tense and glands release hormones that prepare us for fight or flight. In the short term, this is a good thing. When we are exposed to too much noise over the long term, however, those responses can lead to a multitude of health issues, from sleep disturbance to even cardiovascular disease.

声音在进化中帮助人辨认环境和躲避危险，因此突然而响亮的声音会引起血压升高、肌肉紧张和激素释放，为战斗或逃跑做准备。短期内这种反应有保护作用；长期反复承受过量噪声，却可能与睡眠和心血管等健康问题相连。however标出评价变化，变化的关键在暴露的强度和持续时间，而不是所有声音都有害。

B

B The World Health Organization has recently designated excessive noise as an 'underestimated threat' to public health, and has said that people living in cities such as Mumbai, Tokyo and Buenos Aires are being exposed to far more than the recommended 40 decibels of noise at night. A report from the European Environment Agency concluded that noise was an ongoing and widespread issue in Europe, with at least 1 in 5 people consistently exposed to levels considered harmful to health. 'There are no "earlids" that can protect your brain from noise,' says Nick Antonio, an acoustic consultant who has contributed to the British and international standards for noise.

文中引用世界卫生组织和欧洲环境署的说法，将上一段的个体反应扩大为公共健康议题：一些城市的夜间噪声高于文中提到的建议值，欧洲也有相当数量的人持续处于有害噪声水平。声学顾问用没有earlids这一比喻说明，人不像闭眼那样能简单关闭听觉。这些数值与recently都是原文写作时期的描述，不代表实时更新的统计。

C

C The good news is that several cities have been working to turn the volume down. One of the first to do so was London. 'By providing recommendations for quieter buses, reducing noise from roads and also controlling noise from aircraft, they were able to make the city quieter,' says Antonio. Other cities have introduced noise-reducing road coatings, for instance, alongside greenery that muffles sound. Some solutions are more specific: Washington DC's ban on petrol-powered leaf blowers came into effect recently, while in New York City, legislation has been approved to fine people who modify their vehicles to make them noisier. 'People are seeing the benefits of these more quiet environments in their cities,' Antonio says. 'I expect we will see much more of this in the future.'

作者转向城市已经采取的改善措施：伦敦从公交、道路和飞机噪声入手，其他城市采用低噪声路面与绿化，还有城市针对吹叶机或人为改响车辆立法。段落从综合政策写到具体噪声来源，说明公共环境可以通过设计和管理改变。最后关于未来会有更多行动的说法是Antonio的期待，不是已经发生的事实。

词语与搭配

finely attuned to noise

对噪声非常敏感

be attuned to表示敏锐察觉或适应某种信号；finely加强感知的精细程度。

in response to them

作为对它们的反应

in response to引出反应的触发因素；them回指响亮或出乎意料的声音。

an ongoing and widespread issue

一个持续存在且影响广泛的问题

ongoing说明时间上的持续，widespread说明涉及范围大，两者从不同维度描述问题。

reducing noise from roads

减少来自道路的噪声

from说明噪声来源；这里属于城市治理措施之一，表达的是降低噪声，而非把所有道路移除。

greenery that muffles sound

能够减弱声音的绿化植被

muffle是使声音变低、变闷，不能理解为完全隔绝；that从句说明这里提到绿化的功能。

句子精读

When we are exposed to too much noise over the long term, however, those responses can lead to a multitude of health issues, from sleep disturbance to even cardiovascular disease.

然而，当我们长期暴露于过量噪声时，这些反应可能引发多种健康问题，从睡眠受扰，甚至到心血管疾病。

When从句同时限定过量噪声与长期暴露。those responses回指前文血压、肌肉和激素的变化；can lead to表示可能的后果，不是每次暴露都会产生疾病。from...to...列出不同程度的健康问题，however把短期保护作用与长期风险连接起来。

Some solutions are more specific: Washington DC's ban on petrol-powered leaf blowers came into effect recently, while in New York City, legislation has been approved to fine people who modify their vehicles to make them noisier.

一些措施更加具体：华盛顿特区对汽油动力吹叶机的禁令近期开始生效，而纽约市则已批准立法，对改装车辆使其更吵的人处以罚款。

冒号后给出两座城市的实例，while在此并列对照两项政策，并非说明同时发生。to fine交代立法的目的；who修饰people，to make them noisier说明改装造成的变化，them指车辆。recently以原文叙述时间为参照。

这篇材料里可用于写作的表达

reducing noise from roads

减少道路噪声

适合说明鼓励公共交通、步行或骑行可能带来的生活环境收益。需要具体写出减少何种车流或噪声源，不把交通方式改变等同于必然消除所有噪声。

用于写作：题目讨论鼓励替代交通与限制车辆使用；道路噪声是与车辆使用直接相关的生活环境理由。

noise from aircraft

飞机产生的噪声

可用于旅游活动对机场附近居民的影响，须说明航班增长这一具体联系；不能把所有旅游目的地的主要问题一律写成航空噪声。

用于写作：题目明确要求考虑旅游对当地居民与环境的影响；条件句把表达限定在航空活动增长的目的地。

The World of Sugar｜劳动组织与行业权力未作答选词摘要填空 · 2 段 · 203 词 · 6 题 · 同篇原文另有裁切

Complete the summary using the list of words A–I. Write the correct letter A–I. 原选项完整保留；Q31–36。

原文第4段The World of Sugar is also a story of similarity and continuity in sugar cultivation. For example, imported labour has been used for much large-scale production. German beet fields employed Polish workers; Mexicans and many others, including Sicilians, were vital to US sugar production. Cane cutting, Bosma shows, remains a poorly paid and brutal business to this day in many places in the world. But as well as this, the book is about the continuity of the use of traditional methods on small farms. In the mid 20th-century, this type of sugar production dominated in South Asia and Latin America.

原文第5段This is also a history of capitalists and sugar dynasties, as well as corporations that in some cases have remained influential over very long periods. Great firms and great interests have had profound influence on the policies of states. In many places - not just the British Caribbean but Cuba and the Philippines too - a powerful sugar bourgeoisie played a major role in politics and their interests were consequently protected by trade barriers and subsidies. In the battle for control of the industry, it was inevitably the poor countries which came off worse. All this is explored by Bosma with wonderful subtlety and control.

对照答案，回到证据

第 31 题 · H

波兰人赴德、墨西哥人等赴美均是跨地迁移劳工，概括为migrant workers。

German beet fields employed Polish workers; Mexicans and many others, including Sicilians, were vital to US sugar production

第 32 题 · E

small farms与small-scale cultivation对应；F outdated带有落后评价，原文只说traditional。

第 33 题 · I

核对原答案页

材料精读 · 内容与词句

这部分将糖业的连续性放在两个层面观察：劳动者的处境和传统生产方式延续，资本、企业与国家政策的关系也长期存在。书评由田间劳动转向政治经济，解释谁能够保护自己的利益，谁更容易承担代价。

原文第4段

The World of Sugar is also a story of similarity and continuity in sugar cultivation. For example, imported labour has been used for much large-scale production. German beet fields employed Polish workers; Mexicans and many others, including Sicilians, were vital to US sugar production. Cane cutting, Bosma shows, remains a poorly paid and brutal business to this day in many places in the world.
